column8: Wed 18 Nov: store; reference for rows 2-4 (the IPCC's official Chinese scale, mainland characters); the report quotes no Chinese terms, so it serves 3c only as the source behind row 2.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c (and 3e), the sharpest reason the range carries no likelihood word: the IPCC's Chinese prints unlikely as 不可能 and 51% of Study 1 read it as zero (modal answer, re-read at source today; the authors call it simply an error); mainland text, so check TCCIP's Taiwan rendering of unlikely before applying it to Taiwan.
Wed 18 Nov: the same fact as row 2 with its date; carry still printed in AR6 (2021) as row 2's clause, worded as flagged by Harris et al., not as the IPCC's own admission.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, why SKELETON's fallback virtually certain needs its number beside it: Chinese medians 86.5% and 80% (re-read at source today), very likely 70%, likely 50%; the Chinese twin of Q4c-013 and Q4c-019.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Chinese readers nearer 50% and less agreed (6% and 9% ordered the terms as the IPCC does); a difference of size, not kind (Q4c-019), so a clause at most beside row 4.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, the quotable backing for a dollar range with no likelihood word: numbers obviate translation (both quotes re-read at source today); the authors scope it to intergovernmental communication, and the currency must still be named.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, the one Chinese certainty word heard alike by everyone (一定 median 100%, IQR 0) while 可能 sits at 52%; backs plain certain with the stated range as its subject, never on a figure; 52 Beijing postgraduates, mainland script.
Wed 18 Nov: store, the mechanism behind row 7 (likely, probable and possible all become 可能; Sui's two phrases re-read at source today); it rests on Xu and Li (2007), not read, so source 4.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, backs plain certain over almost certain; fix: compare medians with medians (100% against 80-86.5%, about 14-20 points), not a mean of 98%, label it Keel arithmetic across two studies, and say certain with the stated range as its subject, never the stated ends or a figure.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; cross-study, clinical English, abstract only; fix the arithmetic: 18 points of 70 is about a quarter, not a fifth; row 7 already carries the point.
Wed 18 Nov: store; 可能 used for 20% to 95% in production (abstract and Harris's citation only); note it is speakers' usage, while row 7's IQR of 9 is listeners' reading, so the two do not conflict.
Wed 18 Nov: 3d, co-sponsors will want figures from Laura even if they retell them in words, so the figures are what she hands over; abstract read, mainland sample.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, Taiwan's own AR6 summary has no fixed word list (very likely rendered two ways), so any likelihood word is translated case by case; also the check row 2 needs for Taiwan's rendering of unlikely.
Wed 18 Nov: 3c, confidence has no single Chinese word (信度 against 信心), which supports a stated range with no confidence label (never 95% or confidence interval); statistics terms not checked.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, the only Taiwan-sample source on the card, a Taiwanese reason for the rule already in SKELETON 3d (no about before the counted top); holds only if about is rendered 大概 rather than 約, which no source shows; abstract only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c and 3d, why nothing is stated before the move: a likelihood rises as it is retold, and the fix is the source's number, which the owned dollar figures are; clarify the 70-75% clause at source before use; passages only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, Taiwan's public already hears probability as N of 100 similar cases, the frequency form the register uses before the move; a supporting fact beside H9-139, never a weather parallel in the prose.

Wed 18 Nov: same CWA product and the same lesson (say what the band is not); the cone is a 70% probability band while the range after the move is no band at all, so it breaks as a parallel; one row carries it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or Table 2's note, a form model for a what-this-figure-does-not-tell-you list (building costs, the Taiwan dollar); beside Table 3's what-it-never-changes column, a model only, not prose.
Wed 18 Nov: the Taiwan version of the reference-class point H9-139 holds (say what a probability is out of); weather, not money; serves no part on its own.
Wed 18 Nov: store for 3d, 以上 includes the number by statute; the base for row 23, with no Chinese wording proposed for Laura.
Wed 18 Nov: same meaning of 以上 extended to other laws by custom; the ministry letter is secondary only; one clause under row 21.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, the Mandarin at-least words do what Q52 found in English, so the top is said as the plain figure and the bottom once as the part held since January 2028; a restatement of Q52-033 and Q71-035, Keel's reading, no listener test.
Wed 18 Nov: store for 3d, 核定 is the word that makes a grant figure firm in Taiwan (備查 only files it); context for co-sponsors' habits beside Q11d-002 and Q55-008, never wording for Laura.

Wed 18 Nov: store; true of the statute, but everyday 保證 is wider, so adds a guarantor overreaches; it is never a reason to drop guaranteed for Treasuries in the English report (Book 19, no barring a US default).

Wed 18 Nov: 3c and 3d, Taiwan's own fund law (arts 44-45, re-read at source today) bars a fund protected only by its holdings from guaranteed, safe or risk-free, the house rule in Taiwanese law: the certainty word goes on the Treasuries and the stated range, never on IBTM's payout; never protected or capital-protected for the plan.
Wed 18 Nov: same regime as row 26 (art. 19 on names re-read at source today; every cover says not risk-free); one clause under row 26.
Wed 18 Nov: store, the Mandarin twin of the capital-protected ban (保本, at least 90% of principal, art. 44 re-read today); a word kept out of any retelling, never in the report.
Wed 18 Nov: store; 承諾 is a contract's acceptance in law, which serves no part since Laura's words are English and 3d says once whether her figure binds; Q83-024 holds the binding pledge words.

Wed 18 Nov: store; fix the use: no figure is stated before the move (NUMBERS 4), so there is no pre-move range to compare, and SKELETON 3d keeps binding a reader's habit, never a legal question for Laura.
Wed 18 Nov: 3d, evidence for row 32: Taiwan's grant rules write a funder's ceiling as 上限 or 最高; the caps themselves are stored (H9-116, Q49-031), new here is the word.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, the natural Mandarin for the top of a range, 上限, is heard as at most and usually less, so the top is said as the plain figure co-sponsors count, never as a cap or up to (with Q71-010); Keel's inference, no listener test; say every tested future, not every path.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, co-sponsors' habit (figures re-read at source today: 1,081 of 3,141, 49.27% of what funded applicants asked); fix: an ask is not a promise, so drop unlike any figure they usually hear and use it only for why the top is said as committed.

Wed 18 Nov: store; fix: say certain with the stated range as its subject, never the stated ends, and drop firmer than any Taiwanese grant figure, since the 6% not paid in full are cut for grantees' own shortfalls (the card's disanalogy); 2023 figure from an excerpt.
Wed 18 Nov: 3d, a Taiwanese reason for SKELETON 3d's rule (no intend, expect, hope or aim on the top): in grant rules 預估 is a figure re-priced later; 預計 is Keel's extension, one rule read.
Wed 18 Nov: Q83-026 already lists NTPU's 認捐書; the new detail (the form goes with the money) refines Q83-026's pencil reading and belongs there as a clause.
Wed 18 Nov: NT$3.77m against the NT$3m cap is Q11d-032's scale check; the 萬 units add nothing a part needs, and an NT$ figure is never the plan's (SKELETON 3d's one dated NT$ size).
